title: Steady-state Regression Sentinel for Pull Request Benchmarks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Flaky or noisy performance regressions in PRs cause either missed regressions or excessive false positives. Existing CI smoke benches are brittle for short-lived microbursts and cold-start variability. Goal: Build a "steady-state regression sentinel" to run as part of PR gating that produces stable, comparable throughput/latency baselines (tokens/sec, p95 latencies) and emits deterministic pass/fail decisions with explainable signals for on-call and PR reviewers.

Scope & Acceptance criteria:
- Integrate a lightweight harness into PR CI that runs a controlled steady-state workload for a configurable window (default 45s with 15s warmup trimming).
- Compute tokens/sec and p95 distributions per run and compare against a rolling baseline anchored to the canonical release baseline.
- Use a hybrid statistical decision rule (bootstrap CIs on medians + nonparametric rank test) to reduce sensitivity to heavy tails. Fail PR if a regression exceeds both a practical threshold (e.g., >7% regression in tokens/sec or >10% increase in p95) and is statistically significant at alpha=0.05.
- Minimum sample size enforcement (>= 6 independent runs per PR) to reduce flakiness.
- Produce an automated verdict JSON + human-friendly summary in CI logs with links to the baseline dashboard, raw traces, and PR-level comparison plots.

Design notes:
- Workload shape: steady stream of 32-token completions (typical production median length) with KV-cache warm path exercised at 20% of requests. This emphasizes steady-state kernel scheduling rather than transient compile jitter.
- Warmup trimming: first 15s excluded to avoid JIT/compile noise; p95 computed over trimmed window.
- Baseline maintenance: rolling baseline updated weekly using canary runs from dedicated capacity; baseline version pinned per release so historical comparisons remain reproducible.
- Decision rule rationale: simple deterministic thresholds alone cause either too many false alarms or missed regressions depending on noise. Combining effect-size thresholds with a statistical test prevents spurious failures while still catching meaningful performance degradation.

Telemetry & dashboard links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/CI+Steady+State+Sentinel
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://corp-redwood.net/dashboards/steady-sentinel (raw + diff views)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4319

Risks & trade-offs:
- Running longer steady-state tests increases CI runtime cost and feedback latency for reviewers. Mitigation: default short window (45s) and opt-in expanded runs for high-risk components.
- Strict thresholds could block infra churn (e.g., kernel swaps). Mitigation: automatic fallbacks that mark a PR as "needs human review" if upstream infra changes are detected (kernel upgrade tag), plus a canary release channel.

Open questions:
- Exact threshold tuning (7% tokens/sec / 10% p95) requires calibration across model families and GPU types. We will parameterize thresholds per model family.
- Should we gate on a composite scoreboard (tokens/sec + p95 + error-rate) rather than single-metric fails? Proposal: composite scoring in a follow-up.

Acceptance tests:
1) Submit PR with synthetic 12% tokens/sec regression -> CI should fail and link to diff plot.
2) Submit PR that increases p95 by 8% but not statistically significant -> CI should pass but annotate a warning.
3) Run baseline update pipeline and verify weekly baseline rotation does not change historical verdicts (baseline pinned per release).
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created initial ticket after repeated flaky perf gates on ENG infra work. Sketch of steady-state approach and decision rule included. Assigned to Diego for implementation lead.

2026-03-03 - Diego Morales: Spike complete. Prototype harness (bench/steady_load) inside runtime repo can run headless against pinned model artifacts. Early runs show ~12% variance in tokens/sec on riffed kernels when warmup not trimmed.
2026-03-05 - Lena Thompson (PM): Recommend default window 45s with 15s warmup based on production queueing patterns. Also requested an opt-out label for experimental PRs to avoid blocking.

2026-03-07 - Diego Morales: Implemented warmup trimming and bootstrap CI on median. Observed drop in false positives from ~18% -> ~6% on a corpus of 120 historical PR runs. Pushed prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4319

2026-03-08 - Ops review (Rajesh Kapoor): Noted that KV cache priming is a major source of variation when request ratio to cached keys changes. Proposal: fix cache hit ratio to 20% during harness and record hit-rate in verdict metadata.
2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Integrated minimum sample enforcement and per-PR run retries (up to 2 extra runs if high variance detected). Added CI artifact uploader for raw traces and perf histograms.

2026-03-11 - Design feedback (Maya Lin): Dashboard charts look good; requested clearer narrative text when a PR is flagged (why it failed, recommended remediation steps). Added a templated failure summary to CI logs.

2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Beta rollout to infra-team PRs for one week. Observed one true regression (kernel scheduling change) detected and blocked; saved follow-up incident analysis link: https://confluence.redwood/INCIDENTS/2026-03-kernel-sched. Next: parameterize thresholds per model family and add composite metric scoreboard.
